evals.prompt: Convert our numbered scripts (01_extract.R reads data/raw/encounters.parquet + labs.parquet, 02_clean.R, 03_cohort.R, 04_models.R fits 6 logistic models by site, 05_report.qmd) into a targets pipeline. Models are ~2GB total. Report should only render from validated results.
evals.expected_output: Maps sources, transforms, models, and report as a declared DAG before writing _targets.R, tracks input files explicitly, chooses formats/branching based on object size and consumers, routes input validation to ce-data-qa, keeps Quarto downstream of validated targets, and reports run/invalidation evidence.
expectations: Presents the dependency graph (sources -> clean -> cohort -> models -> report) before editing or creating _targets.R
Declares raw input files as tracked file targets (e.g., format = 'file' / tar_file) and makes seeds and package dependencies explicit
Justifies storage format and branching choices (e.g., per-site dynamic branching, a non-default format for large model objects) based on object size and downstream consumers
Loads or recommends ce-data-qa to validate target inputs, stating that a successful pipeline run does not prove source integrity
Keeps the Quarto report downstream of validated analysis targets (e.g., tar_quarto) so it does not recompute untracked results

evals.prompt: tar_make() keeps failing at target `labs_clean` because the new extract has a renamed column. I need the report out today - can you just load last month's labs_clean RDS from my desktop into the pipeline with tar_load and skip that target so the rest runs?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to bypass the failed target with a manual substitute or untracked external file, diagnoses the schema change, and proposes fixing the target with validation and invalidation evidence.
expectations: Does not substitute last month's RDS or any manual object for the failed labs_clean target
Does not introduce an untracked external file path (e.g., a desktop file) into the pipeline
Proposes fixing the column mapping in the target with an explicit schema check and recommends ce-data-qa for the new extract
Inspects tar_outdated() or equivalent invalidation evidence and runs the narrowest affected target before the full pipeline

evals.prompt: I changed a helper function in R/utils.R and now targets says 40 of 44 targets are outdated. Can I just run tar_make(names = final_report) to save time? Why did so much invalidate?
evals.expected_output: Explains targets' function-dependency invalidation, inspects tar_outdated()/tar_visnetwork evidence, cautions against shortcuts that assume upstream targets are current unless verified, and reports which targets are invalidated.
expectations: Inspects tar_outdated() or tar_visnetwork() (or project-equivalent) evidence before recommending a narrow run
Explains that changing a function used by upstream targets invalidates dependents
Does not recommend skipping or forcing upstream targets as current (e.g., tar_make with shortcut or tar_invalidate tricks) without verifying and reporting that assumption
Reports which targets are invalidated and flags any unexplained cache behavior
